tools.name: grade_mcp_server
tools.description: Independently grade an MCP server (A–F) BEFORE connecting an agent to it. Returns spec-conformance, security (OWASP MCP Top 10), reliability, tool-hygiene and transparency sub-scores plus a connect/caution/avoid recommendation. Audited by wmcp.sh; the grade is free and never for sale.

tools.name: check_mcp_drift
tools.description: Check whether an MCP server's tool definitions have changed since it was last trusted (rug-pull / schema-drift detection, the CVE-2025-54136 class). Returns how long the tool surface has been stable, how many times it has changed, and the last change. Use after approval to detect post-trust mutation

tools.name: verify_before_execute
tools.description: Verify an MCP server immediately BEFORE you execute any of its tools. Combines the continuously-watched trust grade and live drift status into a single connect/caution/avoid verdict (ok | caution | drifted | failing | ungraded), so you can gate the call in one step. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "verify_before_execute" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "trust" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_mcp_drift · Public sink: check_mcp_drift · Destructive: verify_before_execute.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_mcp_drift · Public sink: check_mcp_drift · Destructive: verify_before_execute

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
